solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One time in Italy revert to previous speed

parts.note: one as the indefinite article, a
tempo is the Italian word for time

explanation.surface: Someone in Italy is told to slow back down to their earlier pace.
explanation.walkthrough: A TEMPO is the musical instruction to return to the previous speed after a change.
explanation.definitionFit: This musical direction tells players to go back to the original pace after a departure from it.

clue.text: Sycophancy to dismay eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of the preceding words are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Fawning flattery is said to bring about an odd kind of dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being a toady is fawning flattery, which is sycophancy by another name.

clue.text: Old way to serve as a soldier and fight for a cause

definitions.text: Old way to serve as a soldier
definitions.meaning: an archaic sense of the verb was to serve in the army
in modern use the verb means to work or argue in favour of something

explanation.surface: A one-time soldier also campaigns for a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb comes from the Latin for soldiering; it once meant serving as one and now means to weigh in for a cause.

clue.text: Person one joined for better or for worse or for health rundown

definitions.text: Person one joined for better or for worse

indicators.note: a rundown is a breakdown or summary, signalling the preceding letters are broken down and reassembled

explanation.surface: A spouse, married in sickness and in health, gets a medical report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rundown' rearranges FOR HEALTH; the definition echoes the marriage vow 'for better, for worse'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal name for one's spouse, the person married with those wedding vows.

clue.text: One has difficulty seeing through such a downpour

definitions.text: One has difficulty seeing through such
definitions.meaning: a clouding of the eye's lens that impairs vision
a heavy fall of water, as a large waterfall or deluge of rain

explanation.surface: Heavy rain makes it hard to see through.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an eye condition clouding the lens and a torrent or great waterfall.

clue.text: Very calm and unexcited like hothouse plant surprisingly

definitions.meaning: a common simile for staying composed under pressure
read literally the simile compares a person with a salad vegetable grown under glass, which oddly is not chilly at all

explanation.surface: Someone stays utterly unflustered, oddly resembling a greenhouse plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'surprisingly' is the joke: the vegetable in the simile is grown in a warm hothouse, yet it is the byword for coolness.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone who stays perfectly composed and unruffled.

clue.text: Any exit taken out of nervous apprehension

indicators.note: taken out suggests the letters are pulled apart and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Any way out is denied, leaving a sense of nervous dread.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a synonym for worry or unease about what may happen.

clue.text: A new growth Henry, sailor, and I found in the capital

parts.note: a bud is a new shoot on a plant
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A list of a shoot, a man called Henry, a sailor and the speaker, all found in a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the capital of the United Arab Emirates.

clue.text: A time one's entering plant and finding work

indicators.note: entering signals that the group of letters goes inside the plant

parts.note: a tree is a plant
one is I, and one's is I plus S

explanation.surface: Someone takes a moment to enter a factory and finds employment there.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a written work, a formal study of a subject.

clue.text: Pair of spectacles taken after dance at youth hostel causing confusion

indicators.note: taken after places the spectacles behind the dance and hostel pieces, in that order

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
YH is the abbreviation for youth hostel
two round lenses look like the letters O and O

explanation.surface: Someone puts on glasses after a dance at a hostel, causing a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pair of spectacles' is a crossword picture: two round lenses look like a pair of Os.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballyhoo is noisy fuss and commotion, a fair synonym for confusion.

clue.text: Bring up again the smell in the river

indicators.note: in signals that the smell is placed inside the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A bad smell rising from the river is brought up again.
explanation.walkthrough: HUM is informal British for a stink; the EXE is a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhume is to dig up a buried body, so to bring it up once more.

clue.text: The man's row at the back reportedly causing wild excitement

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the phrase is said aloud to give the entry

parts.words: The man's row at the back
parts.note: the man's is HIS, row is TIER, at the back is REAR, giving his-tier-rear

explanation.surface: A man's back row at an event is reported to cause frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'his tier rear' sounds like the word for frenzied excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysteria is uncontrolled emotion, a state of wild excitement or panic.

clue.text: Excited revolutionary more than just warm

parts.note: a red is a communist or revolutionary
hot is beyond merely warm

explanation.surface: An agitated revolutionary is more than a little heated.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-hot can mean intensely passionate or excited, as well as glowing with heat.

clue.text: Rip off the villain

definitions.note: a reckless young troublemaker or hooligan

parts.note: to rip is to tear
away means off, as in gone or absent

explanation.surface: A villain tears something off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rip off' looks like one phrase meaning swindle; it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearaway is a reckless, unruly young person, a hooligan or villain.

clue.text: Craftsman, if erratic, breaks down

indicators.note: breaks down signals the preceding letters are taken apart and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An unreliable craftsman suffers a breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificer is a skilled maker or mechanic, so a craftsman.

clue.text: Disorientated seamen mislaying a name for the duck

indicators.note: disorientated means confused or turned about, so the remaining letters are shuffled
mislaying means losing, so the letters for a and name are dropped

explanation.surface: Confused sailors lose a name for a water bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A and N from SEAMEN to leave SEME, then 'Disorientated' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Smee is a dialect name for a duck such as the smew or wigeon.

clue.text: Careless hit, it's a blow

parts.note: to slap is to hit
a dash is a heavy striking blow, as of waves against rocks

explanation.surface: Someone is struck carelessly and calls it a setback.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash means hasty and careless in one's work.

clue.text: Previous partner Penny allowed to be outspoken

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
licit means lawful or permitted

explanation.surface: An ex named Penny is permitted to speak frankly.
explanation.definitionFit: Explicit speech is frank and direct, so outspoken.

clue.text: Mention some organic items

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone refers to a few organic products.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite is to refer to or quote, a synonym of mention.

clue.text: Went on an expedition and found rude cads rioting

indicators.note: rioting means running wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone travelled abroad and met ill-mannered men running riot.
explanation.definitionFit: To crusade is to go on a campaign or military expedition, originally to the Holy Land.

clue.text: Acquire a route from restaurant

parts.note: to take is to acquire
a way is a route

explanation.surface: Someone gets directions out of a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a takeaway is a restaurant selling food to eat elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A takeaway is a shop or restaurant that sells cooked food to be eaten off the premises.

clue.text: In an excited state has a small speculation

parts.note: a flutter is British slang for a small bet

explanation.surface: Someone is all excited about a little gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: A FLUTTER is British slang for a modest bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Aflutter means agitated or nervously excited.

clue.text: Magazine found on the Piccadilly Line

definitions.meaning: a station on this London Underground line, serving the football ground

explanation.surface: A periodical is found on a London Tube line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Piccadilly Line is a London Underground line with a station of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a store of weapons and also names a station on that Tube line.

clue.text: Eastern European — or French?

definitions.meaning: French ... is a high-gloss finish for wood

explanation.surface: Is someone from eastern Europe, or from France?
explanation.walkthrough: French polish is a glossy shellac finish for furniture, so French precedes the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the adjective for Poland, and with French in front names a wood finish.

clue.text: Open feast nun prepared

indicators.note: prepared suggests the letters are made ready in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A nun has made ready a feast for an opening.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten is to undo or open something.

clue.text: A second amount of money on the way up

parts.note: a cent is a small coin or sum

explanation.surface: Someone has a further sum of money and is going up in the world.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is a climb, a route going upward.

clue.text: Surrender face up

definitions.meaning: to concede or give way in an argument
lying face up means lying on one's back

explanation.surface: Give in and face the music.
explanation.walkthrough: Lying face up is lying with your back downward; the more obvious 'face up to' is the opposite of surrender.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to give way or retreat from a position, and read literally describes lying face upward.

clue.text: Person who is accommodating

parts.note: accommodating looks like obliging or helpful, but here means providing rooms for guests

explanation.surface: A helpful, obliging person.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotelier runs a hotel, literally providing accommodation for guests.

clue.text: Rudd's colourful feature

parts.note: the rudd is a freshwater fish whose eyes are a vivid red, giving it an alternative name

explanation.surface: Someone named Rudd has a striking colourful trait.
explanation.walkthrough: Rudd looks like a surname; it is a European freshwater fish with red eyes, and is also called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The rudd fish has bright red eyes and is also known by this hyphenated name.
